To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) RGB-D pedestrian detection is a promising research direction, (b) depth cues can improve pedestrian detection performance by a factor of 1.5, (c) the performance of the RGB-D system depends on how depth is fused with the RGB image and on the quality of the depth map, (d) the best performing RGB-D system is the one that fuses depth and color in a context-dependent manner.

a) depth cues are a very promising midlevel target for pedestrian detection, b) the use of depth information can improve detection performance, c) depth upsampling is a key step in the process, and d) depth and RGB cues can be combined in a very efficient way.

(1) the combination of RGB and depth information improves pedestrian detection accuracy by 2-4% over the RGB-only case, depending on the depth quality, and (2) the best performance is achieved by fusing the depth information in the context of a deformable parts detector, which allows for the detection of pedestrians in a variety of poses.
